```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE

# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
library(lubridate)
library(broom)
library(knitr)


# Step 1 Load Dataset

cancer_trials <- read_csv(
  "cancer_trials_2020_2024.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

#Data Checks

# View column names
names(cancer_trials)

# View structure
str(cancer_trials)

# View first rows
head(cancer_trials)

# Number of rows and columns
dim(cancer_trials)


#Missing Data

missing_values <- cancer_trials %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      everything(),
      ~ sum(is.na(.x))
    )
  )

missing_values


#Duplicate Data

duplicate_summary <- cancer_trials %>%
  summarise(
    duplicate_rows = sum(duplicated(.))
  )

duplicate_summary


#Standardise Duration_Days

cancer_trials <- cancer_trials %>%
  mutate(
    # Convert dates to character first
    start_date = as.character(start_date),
    completion_date = as.character(completion_date),

    # Add first day of month when only YYYY-MM is supplied
    start_date = if_else(
      str_detect(start_date, "^\\d{4}-\\d{2}$"),
      paste0(start_date, "-01"),
      start_date
    ),

    completion_date = if_else(
      str_detect(completion_date, "^\\d{4}-\\d{2}$"),
      paste0(completion_date, "-01"),
      completion_date
    ),

    # Convert to R Date format
    start_date = ymd(start_date),
    completion_date = ymd(completion_date),

    # Calculate duration
    duration_days = as.numeric(
      completion_date - start_date
    )
  )


# Check duration
summary(cancer_trials$duration_days)


#Zero-Days in DUration Check

zero_duration_trials <- cancer_trials %>%
  filter(duration_days == 0)

nrow(zero_duration_trials)

# Remove zero-day trials while KEEPING NA duration rows
cancer_trials <- cancer_trials %>%
  filter(is.na(duration_days) | duration_days > 0)

nrow(cancer_trials)


#Standardise Clinical Trial Phases

cancer_trials <- cancer_trials %>%
  mutate(
    phase_standardised = case_when(

      # NA or blank = phase not required
      is.na(phase) ~ "Phase Not Required",

      str_trim(phase) == "" ~ "Phase Not Required",

      # Phase IV checked first
      str_detect(
        str_to_upper(phase),
        "PHASE ?4|PHASE IV"
      ) ~ "Phase IV",

      # Phase III checked before Phase II
      str_detect(
        str_to_upper(phase),
        "PHASE ?3|PHASE III"
      ) ~ "Phase III",

      # Phase II checked before Phase I
      str_detect(
        str_to_upper(phase),
        "PHASE ?2|PHASE II"
      ) ~ "Phase II",

      str_detect(
        str_to_upper(phase),
        "EARLY_PHASE1|EARLY PHASE 1"
      ) ~ "Phase I",

      str_detect(
        str_to_upper(phase),
        "PHASE ?1|PHASE I"
      ) ~ "Phase I",

      str_detect(
        str_to_upper(phase),
        "NOT SPECIFIED"
      ) ~ "Not Specified",

      str_detect(
        str_to_upper(phase),
        "NOT REQUIRED|RX NOT REQUIRED"
      ) ~ "Phase Not Required",

      TRUE ~ "Not Specified"
    )
  )


#Phase Frequency Table

phase_frequency <- cancer_trials %>%
  count(
    phase_standardised,
    name = "Frequency"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = round(
      Frequency / sum(Frequency) * 100,
      2
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(
    match(
      phase_standardised,
      c(
        "Phase I",
        "Phase II",
        "Phase III",
        "Phase IV",
        "Not Specified",
        "Phase Not Required"
      )
    )
  )

phase_frequency

kable(
  phase_frequency,
  caption = "Frequency Distribution of Clinical Trial Phases"
)


#Standardise Intervention

cancer_trials <- cancer_trials %>%
  mutate(

    intervention_standardised = case_when(

      # Missing or blank values
      is.na(intervention_types) |
        str_trim(intervention_types) == "" ~
        "Intervention Not Specified",

      # Multiple interventions
      str_detect(
        intervention_types,
        "[,;|]"
      ) ~ "Multiple Interventions",

      # Individual categories
      str_to_upper(
        str_trim(intervention_types)
      ) == "DRUG" ~ "Drug",

      str_to_upper(
        str_trim(intervention_types)
      ) == "BIOLOGICAL" ~ "Biological",

      str_to_upper(
        str_trim(intervention_types)
      ) == "PROCEDURE" ~ "Procedure",

      str_to_upper(
        str_trim(intervention_types)
      ) == "DEVICE" ~ "Device",

      str_to_upper(
        str_trim(intervention_types)
      ) == "RADIATION" ~ "Radiation",

      str_to_upper(
        str_trim(intervention_types)
      ) %in%
        c("BEHAVIORAL", "BEHAVIOURAL") ~
        "Behavioural",

      str_to_upper(
        str_trim(intervention_types)
      ) == "DIAGNOSTIC_TEST" ~
        "Diagnostic Test",

      str_to_upper(
        str_trim(intervention_types)
      ) == "DIETARY_SUPPLEMENT" ~
        "Dietary Supplement",

      str_to_upper(
        str_trim(intervention_types)
      ) == "GENETIC" ~ "Genetic",

      str_to_upper(
        str_trim(intervention_types)
      ) %in%
        c(
          "COMBINATION_PRODUCT",
          "COMBINATION_PRODUCTS"
        ) ~
        "Combination Product",

      str_to_upper(
        str_trim(intervention_types)
      ) == "OTHER" ~ "Other",

      TRUE ~ "Unclassified"
    )
  )


#Intervention Frequency Table

intervention_frequency <- cancer_trials %>%
  count(
    intervention_standardised,
    name = "Frequency"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Percentage = round(
      Frequency / sum(Frequency) * 100,
      2
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Frequency))

intervention_frequency

kable(
  intervention_frequency,
  caption = "Frequency Distribution of Intervention Types"
)


#Standardise Conditions

cancer_trials <- cancer_trials %>%
  mutate(

    condition_standardised = case_when(

      # Missing/blank condition
      is.na(conditions) |
        str_trim(conditions) == "" ~
        "Unspecified Cancer",

      # Multiple cancers
      str_detect(
        conditions,
        "[,;|]"
      ) ~ "Multiple Cancers",

      # Haematological cancers
      str_detect(
        str_to_lower(conditions),
        paste0(
          "leukemia|leukaemia|lymphoma|",
          "myeloma|hematolog|haematolog"
        )
      ) ~ "Haematological Cancers",

      # Brain/CNS cancers
      str_detect(
        str_to_lower(conditions),
        paste0(
          "brain|glioblastoma|glioma|",
          "central nervous system|cns|",
          "medulloblastoma"
        )
      ) ~ "Brain and CNS Cancers",

      # Skin / soft tissue / bone
      str_detect(
        str_to_lower(conditions),
        paste0(
          "melanoma|skin|sarcoma|",
          "bone cancer|osteosarcoma|",
          "soft tissue"
        )
      ) ~
        "Skin, Soft Tissue and Bone Cancers",

      # Major organ cancers
      str_detect(
        str_to_lower(conditions),
        paste0(
          "breast|lung|prostate|",
          "colorectal|colon|rectal|",
          "pancrea|liver|hepatic|",
          "kidney|renal|ovarian|",
          "cervical|bladder|gastric|",
          "stomach|thyroid|",
          "endometrial|uterine|",
          "oesophag|esophag|",
          "head and neck|oral|testicular"
        )
      ) ~ "Organ Cancers",

      TRUE ~ "Unspecified Cancer"
    )
  )


#Enrollment data checks

enrollment_summary <- cancer_trials %>%
  summarise(
    Mean = round(
      mean(enrollment, na.rm = TRUE),
      2
    ),

    Median = median(
      enrollment,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    Mode = as.numeric(
      names(
        sort(
          table(enrollment),
          decreasing = TRUE
        )[1]
      )
    ),

    Minimum = min(
      enrollment,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    Maximum = max(
      enrollment,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    SD = round(
      sd(enrollment, na.rm = TRUE),
      2
    ),

    Q1 = as.numeric(
      quantile(
        enrollment,
        0.25,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    ),

    Q3 = as.numeric(
      quantile(
        enrollment,
        0.75,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    ),

    IQR = IQR(
      enrollment,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )

enrollment_summary


# Convert to long table
enrollment_table <- enrollment_summary %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Statistic",
    values_to = "Enrollment"
  )

kable(
  enrollment_table,
  caption = "Descriptive Statistics for Clinical Trial Enrollment"
)


#Enrollment Outliers

Q1_enrollment <- quantile(
  cancer_trials$enrollment,
  0.25,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

Q3_enrollment <- quantile(
  cancer_trials$enrollment,
  0.75,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

IQR_enrollment <- (
  Q3_enrollment - Q1_enrollment
)

lower_enrollment <- (
  Q1_enrollment -
    1.5 * IQR_enrollment
)

upper_enrollment <- (
  Q3_enrollment +
    1.5 * IQR_enrollment
)


enrollment_outliers <- cancer_trials %>%
  summarise(

    Total_Trials = n(),

    Valid_Enrollment =
      sum(!is.na(enrollment)),

    Lower_Outliers =
      sum(
        enrollment < lower_enrollment,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    Upper_Outliers =
      sum(
        enrollment > upper_enrollment,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
  ) %>%
  mutate(

    Total_Outliers =
      Lower_Outliers + Upper_Outliers,

    Percentage = round(
      Total_Outliers /
        Valid_Enrollment * 100,
      2
    )
  )

enrollment_outliers


#Enrollment Outlier Table

outlier_table <- tibble(

  Statistic = c(
    "Total clinical trials",
    "Valid enrollment observations",
    "Potential enrollment outliers",
    "Percentage of valid observations",

  ),

  Result = c(

    format(

    ),

    format(
      enrollment_outliers$Total_Outliers,

    ),

      1
    ),

)

kable(

#Duration Outliers

Q1_duration <- quantile(
  cancer_trials$duration_days,
  0.25,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

Q3_duration <- quantile(
  cancer_trials$duration_days,
  0.75,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

IQR_duration <- (
  Q3_duration -
    Q1_duration
)

lower_duration <- (
  Q1_duration -
    1.5 * IQR_duration
)

upper_duration <- (
  Q3_duration +
    1.5 * IQR_duration
)


duration_outliers <- cancer_trials %>%
  summarise(

    Total_Trials = n(),

    Valid_Durations =
      sum(!is.na(duration_days)),

    Lower_Outliers =
      sum(
        duration_days <
          lower_duration,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    Upper_Outliers =
      sum(
        duration_days >
          upper_duration,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
  ) %>%
  mutate(

    Total_Outliers =
      Lower_Outliers +
      Upper_Outliers,

    Percentage =
      round(
        Total_Outliers /
          Valid_Durations * 100,
        2
      ),

    Lower_Threshold =
      as.numeric(
        lower_duration
      ),

    Upper_Threshold =
      as.numeric(
        upper_duration
      )
  )

duration_outliers

# Enrollment Outlier Comparison by Study Type

outlier_comparison <- cancer_trials %>%
  group_by(study_type) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Trials = n(),
    Mean = mean(enrollment, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(enrollment, na.rm = TRUE),
    Q1 = as.numeric(quantile(enrollment, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)),
    Q3 = as.numeric(quantile(enrollment, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)),
    IQR = IQR(enrollment, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Upper_Bound = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    cancer_trials %>%
      group_by(study_type) %>%
      summarise(
        Enrollment_Values = list(enrollment),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = "study_type"
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    Outliers = sum(
      Enrollment_Values < Q1 - 1.5 * IQR |
      Enrollment_Values > Upper_Bound,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    Outlier_Percentage = round(
      100 * Outliers / sum(!is.na(Enrollment_Values)),
      2
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-Enrollment_Values)

outlier_comparison



#Binomial Hypothesis Testing

intervention_data <- cancer_trials %>%
  filter(
    intervention_standardised %in%
      c(
        "Drug",
        "Device",
        "Procedure"
      )
  )


# Count each intervention
intervention_counts <-
  intervention_data %>%
  count(
    intervention_standardised,
    name = "Count"
  )

intervention_counts


# Counts
drug_count <- intervention_counts %>%
  filter(
    intervention_standardised == "Drug"
  ) %>%
  pull(Count)

device_count <- intervention_counts %>%
  filter(
    intervention_standardised == "Device"
  ) %>%
  pull(Count)

procedure_count <- intervention_counts %>%
  filter(
    intervention_standardised == "Procedure"
  ) %>%
  pull(Count)


other_count <-
  device_count +
  procedure_count


# One-sided binomial test

test_drug_combined <- binom.test(

  x = drug_count,

  n = drug_count +
    other_count,

  p = 0.5,

  alternative = "greater"
)


test_drug_combined


#Binomial Table

binomial_table <- tibble(

  Statistic = c(

    "Statistical Test",

    "Drug Interventions",

    "Device Interventions",

    "Procedure Interventions",

    "Device + Procedure Interventions",

    "Total Included Trials",

    "Drug Proportion (%)",

    "Device + Procedure Proportion (%)",

    "Null Hypothesis Proportion",

    "P-Value",

    "95% Confidence Interval Lower Bound (%)",

    "Significance Level",

    "Hypothesis Decision"
  ),

  Result = c(

    "One-sided Exact Binomial Test",

    format(
      drug_count,
      big.mark = ","
    ),

    format(
      device_count,
      big.mark = ","
    ),

    format(
      procedure_count,
      big.mark = ","
    ),

    format(
      other_count,
      big.mark = ","
    ),

    format(
      drug_count +
        other_count,
      big.mark = ","
    ),

    paste0(
      round(
        test_drug_combined$estimate *
          100,
        2
      ),
      "%"
    ),

    paste0(
      round(
        other_count /
          (drug_count + other_count) *
          100,
        2
      ),
      "%"
    ),

    "50%",

    format.pval(
      test_drug_combined$p.value,
      digits = 3,
      eps = 0.001
    ),

    paste0(
      round(
        test_drug_combined$conf.int[1] *
          100,
        2
      ),
      "%"
    ),

    "0.05",

    if_else(
      test_drug_combined$p.value < 0.05,
      "Reject Null Hypothesis",
      "Fail to Reject Null Hypothesis"
    )
  )
)

kable(
  binomial_table,
  caption = "Binomial Hypothesis Test Results"
)


#Pearson Chi-Square Test

chi_data <- cancer_trials %>%
  filter(

    intervention_standardised %in%
      c(
        "Drug",
        "Device",
        "Procedure"
      ),

    phase_standardised %in%
      c(
        "Phase I",
        "Phase II",
        "Phase III",
        "Phase IV"
      )
  )


# Contingency table

chi_table <- table(

  chi_data$intervention_standardised,

  chi_data$phase_standardised
)

chi_table


# Pearson Chi-square test

chi_test <- chisq.test(
  chi_table
)

chi_test


# Expected frequencies

minimum_expected <- min(
  chi_test$expected
)

percent_below_five <- mean(
  chi_test$expected < 5
) * 100


#Cramer's V Test

cramers_v <- sqrt(

  as.numeric(
    chi_test$statistic
  ) /

    (
      sum(chi_table) *

        (
          min(
            dim(chi_table)
          ) - 1
        )
    )
)


#Chi-Square Table

chi_summary <- tibble(

  Statistic = c(

    "Pearson Chi-square Statistic",

    "Degrees of Freedom",

    "Total Observations",

    "P-Value",

    "Cramér's V",

    "Minimum Expected Frequency",

    "Expected Cells Below 5 (%)",

    "Hypothesis Decision"
  ),

  Result = c(

    round(
      as.numeric(
        chi_test$statistic
      ),
      2
    ),

    as.numeric(
      chi_test$parameter
    ),

    sum(
      chi_table
    ),

    format.pval(
      chi_test$p.value,
      digits = 3,
      eps = 0.001
    ),

    round(
      cramers_v,
      3
    ),

    round(
      minimum_expected,
      2
    ),

    round(
      percent_below_five,
      2
    ),

    if_else(
      chi_test$p.value < 0.05,
      "Reject Null Hypothesis",
      "Fail to Reject Null Hypothesis"
    )
  )
)

kable(
  chi_summary,
  caption = "Pearson Chi-square Test Results"
)


#Logistic Regression

logistic_data <- cancer_trials %>%
  filter(

    intervention_standardised %in%
      c(
        "Drug",
        "Device",
        "Procedure"
      ),

    phase_standardised %in%
      c(
        "Phase I",
        "Phase II",
        "Phase III",
        "Phase IV"
      )
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    Later_Phase = if_else(

      phase_standardised %in%
        c(
          "Phase III",
          "Phase IV"
        ),

      1L,

      0L
    ),

    intervention_standardised =
      factor(

        intervention_standardised,

        levels =
          c(
            "Drug",
            "Device",
            "Procedure"
          )
      )
  )


#Early vs Later Phase Counts

logistic_counts <- logistic_data %>%
  count(
    intervention_standardised,
    Later_Phase
  ) %>%

  pivot_wider(

    names_from = Later_Phase,

    values_from = n,

    names_prefix = "Outcome_",

    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%

  rename(

    Early_Phase =
      Outcome_0,

    Later_Phase =
      Outcome_1
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    Total =
      Early_Phase +
      Later_Phase,

    Later_Phase_Percentage =
      round(
        Later_Phase /
          Total * 100,
        2
      )
  )

logistic_counts

kable(
  logistic_counts,
  caption = "Early and Later Clinical Trial Phases by Intervention Type"
)


#Logistic Regression Model

logistic_model <- glm(

  Later_Phase ~
    intervention_standardised,

  data = logistic_data,

  family =
    binomial(
      link = "logit"
    )
)


summary(
  logistic_model
)


#Logistic Regression Odds Ratio

logistic_results <- broom::tidy(

  logistic_model,

  conf.int = TRUE,

  exponentiate = TRUE

) %>%

  select(

    term,

    estimate,

    conf.low,

    conf.high,

    p.value

  ) %>%

  rename(

    Term = term,

    Odds_Ratio = estimate,

    CI_Lower_95 = conf.low,

    CI_Upper_95 = conf.high,

    P_Value = p.value
  )

logistic_results

kable(
  logistic_results,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Logistic Regression Odds Ratios"
)

# Logistic Regression Comparison Table

logistic_comparison <- logistic_results %>%
  filter(Term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  mutate(
    Intervention = case_when(
      str_detect(Term, "Device") ~ "Device vs Drug",
      str_detect(Term, "Procedure") ~ "Procedure vs Drug",
      TRUE ~ Term
    ),
    Odds_Ratio = round(Odds_Ratio, 2),
    Confidence_Interval = paste0(
      round(CI_Lower_95, 2),
      " - ",
      round(CI_Upper_95, 2)
    ),
    Significant = if_else(
      P_Value < 0.05,
      "Yes",
      "No"
    ),
    Interpretation = if_else(
      P_Value < 0.05,
      "Statistically significant",
      "Not statistically significant"
    )
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    Intervention,
    Odds_Ratio,
    Confidence_Interval,
    P_Value,
    Significant,
    Interpretation
  )

logistic_comparison

#Logistic Regression Model Fit Information

model_fit <- tibble(

  Statistic = c(

    "Number of Observations",

    "Null Deviance",

    "Residual Deviance",

    "AIC"
  ),

  Value = c(

    nobs(
      logistic_model
    ),

    logistic_model$null.deviance,

    logistic_model$deviance,

    AIC(
      logistic_model
    )
  )
)

kable(
  model_fit,
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Logistic Regression Model Fit"
)

```

Cancer remains a significant global health challenge, driving continuous research into the development and evaluation of effective treatment interventions. Clinical trials play a fundamental role in this process by investigating the safety, efficacy, and clinical applications of pharmaceutical drugs, medical devices, and procedural interventions. Clinical research involves different stages of investigations. Phase I trials generally focus on safety, tolerability, and dosage. Phase II trials provide further evidence of safety, and preliminary efficacy. Phase III trials commonly evaluate treatment effectiveness, and safety in larger patient populations. Phase IV trials generally involve post marketing studies of approved cancer interventions. Clinical trial phase classifications are primarily associated with drug and biological product development, and may not be directly required or applicable to observational, device, or procedural clinical studies.

The objectives of this study was to investigate the distribution of cancer clinical trials conducted between 2020 and 2024, with particular attention to intervention type, and clinical trial phase. The analysis seeked to determine whether pharmaceutical drug interventions were more frequently represented than device and procedural interventions, and whether intervention type was associated with classification in later clinical trial phases, particularly Phase III and Phase IV.

The Cancer Clinical Trials 2020–2024 dataset was obtained from Kaggle and contains 10,000 clinical trial records, 14 variables and all completed cancer trial studies. The key features selected for this analysis include nct_id, study_type, phase, conditions, interventions, intervention_types, enrolment, start_date and completion_date. These variables were selected to evaluate clinical trial characteristics, intervention classifications, and clinical development phases, as well as to explore patterns and relationships between participant enrolment, and trial duration. The study applied descriptive statistics, exploratory data analysis, statistical binomial hypothesis testing, and logistic regression modelling.

The Cancer Clinical Trials 2020-2024 dataset was reviewed, cleaned, transformed, and prepared prior to statistical analysis. In particular, there were 1,076 missing days within the dates for start_date, and 534 missing days within the dates for completion_date. These dates were imputed for the first day of the month. The start_date and completion_date variables were converted into duration_days, representing the length of days of each clinical trial. There were 9 observations that had the same start_date and completion_date, indicating that the trial did not commence or there were data quality issues with the date imputations. These 9 observations were removed from the dataset. As a result there were 9991 observations analysed in the dataset for this study. There were 2715 NA observations in the phase variable that were kept and changed to Not Required. The phases were standardised through aggregating into Phase I, Phase II, Phase III, Phase IV, Not Specified, and Not Required, using the later Phase to represent the study Phase. The intervention_studies were standardised through aggregating into Drug, Biological, Procedure, Device, Radiation, Behavioural, Diagnostic_Test, Dietary_Supplement, Genetic, Combination_Products, Other, and Multiple_Interventions, for more than one type of intervention category in the observations. There were 32 different categorical conditions that were standardised and aggregated into 6 categories: Organ Cancers, Haematological Cancers, Brain and CNS Cancers, Skin, Soft Tissue and Bone Cancers, Multiple Cancers, and Unspecified Cancers. There were 903 NA observations in the intervention_type, that were kept and changed to Not Required. There were 905 missing observations in interventions that were kept and changed to Not Required. There were no duplicates in the dataset. R programming language was utilised for the analysis, reporting, and visualisations for this study.

Descriptive analysis focused on identifying the distributions of the Standardised Phases and Intervention Types, while also identifying the central tendencies for Enrolment and Duration_Days. The distribution of standardised clinical trial phases revealed that the largest proportion of studies were classified as Phase Not Required (27.25%, n=2713), followed by Phase Not Specified (26.03%, n= 2603), Phase II (23.48%, n=2346), and Phase I (15.29%, n=1528). In contrast, later stage clinical trials were less prevalent, with Phase III accounting for 6.67% (n=666) and Phase IV representing the smallest proportion at 1.37% (n=137).

Clinical trial enrolment distribution varied considerably across the dataset, ranging from a minimum of 1 participant to a maximum of 36,580,288 participants. The mean enrolment was 9260.02 participants, which was substantially higher than the median 66 participants, and mode 30 participants. The interquartile range (IQR) was 163 participants, indicating considerable variability within the middle 50% of observations. The enrolment variable was evaluated for potential outliers (13.1%, n=1305).

The clinical trial duration's distributions revealed considerable variability. The maximum participant duration was 15705 days and the minimum was 3 days. The mean trial duration was 1659.31 days, exceeding the median of 1294 days, and mode of 730 days. The interquartile range (IQR) was 1525.50 days, indicating a large variation in clinical trial durations among the middle 50% of observations. Exploratory Data Analysis was used to investigate any potential outliers in enrolment and duration. Outliers in enrolment were represented by positive skewing (mean = 9260.02, median = 66), indicating there were large clinical trial enrolments. Enrolment distribution was differentiated by study type. There were 7391 clinical trials enrolled as interventional, with mean 288.28, median 53, IQR 98, and outliers 910 (12.31%). There were 2600 clinical trials enrolled as observational, with mean 34763.93, median 170, IQR 467.75, and outliers 363 (13.96%). However, these outliers did not impact the objectives of the study. The enrolment outliers were not directly included in the statistical modelling of binomial hypothesis testing, Pearson Chi-square testing, or binary logistic regression modelling.

Outliers in duration were represented by positive skewing (mean = 1659.31, median = 1294), indicating there were clinical trials with longer duration days. Outlier's analysis using Tukey’s fences (1.5 × IQR method) identified no potential lower outliers in duration, while 492 clinical trials (4.92%) were classified as potential upper threshold outliers. These findings indicate that extreme duration values were concentrated in the upper tail of the distribution. Outliers in duration were not directly included in the statistical modelling of binomial hypothesis testing, Pearson Chi-square testing, or binary logistic regression modelling.

A statistical one-sided binomial test was conducted to investigate whether Drug interventions were more frequently represented than Device and Procedure interventions combined. Out of the 4369 selected clinical trials, 3287 (75.23%) were classified as Drug interventions, compared with 1082 (24.77%) classified as combined Device or Procedure interventions.

The observed Drug proportion was 0.7523, with a one-sided 95% confidence interval lower bound of 0.7414. The test demonstrated a statistically significant result (p < 0.001), indicating that the observed proportion of Drug interventions was significantly greater than the hypothesised proportion of 0.50. Therefore, the null hypothesis was rejected, providing strong statistical evidence that Drug interventions were more frequently represented than Device and Procedure interventions combined within the clinical trials dataset.

```{r binomial-long-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  binomial_table,
  col.names = c("Statistical Measure", "Result"),
  caption = "One-Sided Binomial Hypothesis Test: Drug vs Device and Procedure Interventions"
)
```
Figure 7.0 Statistical One-Sided Binomial Hypothesis Test


A Pearson Chi-square Test of Independence was conducted to investigate the association between intervention type and clinical trial phase classification among 4369 selected clinical trials. The large chi-square statistics of χ² = 2727.04, and small p value (p <0.001), provided strong statistical evidence against the null hypothesis of independence and for a strong association between the categorical variables: intervention type, and clinical trial phase classifications.  Cramér's V further supported this strong association (V = 0.559).

```{r chi-square-summary-table, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  chi_summary,
  col.names = c("Statistical Measure", "Result"),
  caption = "Pearson Chi-square Test of Independence and Cramér's V"
)
```
Figure 8.0 Pearson Chi-Square Test of Independence and Cramer's V


Binary logistic regression was conducted to investigate whether intervention type was associated with the odds of a clinical trial being classified as Phase III or Phase IV, compared with Phase I or Phase II. The analysis included 2962 clinical trials of Phases I–IV, using Drug interventions as the reference category.

Device interventions demonstrated higher estimated odds of later-phase classification compared with Drug interventions (OR = 2.34, 95% CI: 0.96–5.72). However, this association was not statistically significant at the 5% significance level (p = 0.0624). The confidence interval included the null value of 1, indicating insufficient statistical evidence to establish a difference in odds between Device and Drug interventions.

In contrast, Procedure interventions demonstrated significantly higher odds of later-phase classification compared with Drug interventions (OR = 4.13, 95% CI: 2.18–7.84, p < 0.001). The confidence interval excluded 1, supporting the finding of a statistically significant association. Specifically, Procedure interventions had approximately 4.13 times the odds of being classified as Phase III or IV compared with Drug interventions.

Overall, the analysis identified statistically significant differences in later-phase classification between Procedure and Drug interventions, while the estimated difference between Device and Drug interventions did not reach statistical significance.

Conclusion

The objective of this study was to investigate the distribution of cancer clinical trials conducted between 2020 and 2024, with particular emphasis on intervention type and clinical trial phase classification. The findings provided strong statistical evidence of an association between intervention type and clinical trial phase classification, indicating that the distribution of clinical phases differed significantly across Drug, Device and Procedure interventions. The analysis provided statistically significant evidence that Procedure interventions had higher odds of being classified in later clinical trial phases (Phases III and IV) compared with Drug interventions (OR = 4.13, p < 0.001). Although Device interventions also demonstrated higher estimated odds of later-phase classification (OR = 2.34), this association was not statistically significant (p = 0.0624).

Furthermore, while Drug interventions were significantly more prevalent than Device and Procedure interventions combined in the overall Cancer Clinical Trials 2020-2024 dataset, the analysis did not establish that Drug interventions were more prevalent in the later clinical trial phases (Phases III and IV). Overall, these findings highlight the importance of distinguishing between statistical association and evidence of clinical trial progression. Although intervention type was significantly associated with phase classification, this association does not necessarily indicate that Drug interventions are more likely to advance into later stages of clinical development.
